data.name: Harman
data.gender_notes: Harman is used as a masculine name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: One who protects and provides strength, derived from the Hindu god Hari (Vishnu) and man, meaning mountain. The name Harman carries the meaning “Mountain Force” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Punjabi. Parents who choose Harman usually hope their child will grow to embody mountain force and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name that signifies the presence and protection of the divine.
data.etymology: Harman belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Mountain Force.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Harman total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

data.cultural_impact: Krishna comes from the Sanskrit word krish, meaning "dark" or "black," and the Sanskrit suffix na, meaning "linked with" or "relating to." In Hindu mythology, Krishna is known for his dark complexion and his role as a central deity in the ancient Indian epic Mahabharata and as the chief deity of the Bhagavad Gita. The name holds a significant cultural impact in India and beyond, symbolizing love, poetry, and transcendental wisdom.
data.spiritual_significance: Krishna is one of the fundamental deities in the Hindu pantheon and is a widely revered symbol of divinity in Hinduism. He is considered the eighth avatar of the god Vishnu and is regarded as the supreme God and god of protection, love, and compassion. "Krishna" also refers to several manuscripts and texts associated with Hinduism and Jainism, as well as a branch of Hindu philosophy called Krishnaism. Thus, the name "Krishna" carries immense spiritual significance and has been a source of inspiration and guidance for countless individuals throughout history.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Harman: God's Beloved. One whose soul is deeply connected with and governed by the divine will of Hari (Vishnu).

historical_references.reference: Harman was a prominent Hindu ruler of the Punjab region in the late 15th to early 16th century. He is best known for his resistance against the Mughal invaders led by Babur.

Harman was also a renowned Hindu saint and philosopher, who is believed to have lived in the 11th century. He is a central figure in Nath Yoga tradition and is famous for his teachings on the concept of Shivnetra, or the divine vision of Shiva.
